source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 17 May 1961, p. 7 ("Dungannon")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: the Tyrone unopposed-returns report read in the Belfast News-Letter of 17 May 1961.

note: Triennial election of Dungannon Rural District Council, polled Thursday 1 June 1961. Thirteen Unionists and six Nationalists were returned unopposed. The report names only the two Unionist changes, in Anahoe and Altmore; the other members are not listed. Returned unopposed in place of Mr. Thomas Steen, who did not seek re-election. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Anahoe' to Aghnahoe (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the 1948 order naming Dungannon Rural District's nineteen divisions (Ministry of Health and Local Government, 26 August 1948; Belfast Gazette, 1 April 1949), the DED maps (AGHNAHOE) and the OSNI townland spell it Aghnahoe. This round was filed under the spelling 'Anahoe', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (anahoe) answers with a redirect to this one.
